units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
With his hands before his face, he buries his head in her lap, and breaks into bitter sobbing.
White and trembling.
Oswald! Look at me! No, no; it's not true.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Looks up with despair in his eyes.
Never to be able to work again! Never!--never! A living death! Mother, can you imagine anything so horrible?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: My poor boy! How has this horrible thing come upon you?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Sitting upright again.
That's just what I cannot possibly grasp or understand. I have never led a dissipated life--never, in any respect. You mustn't believe that of me, mother! I've never done that.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: I am sure you haven't, Oswald.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: And yet this has come upon me just the same--this awful misfortune!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Oh, but it will pass over, my dear, blessed boy. It's nothing but over-work. Trust me, I am right.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Sadly.
I thought so too, at first; but it isn't so.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Tell me everything, from beginning to end.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes, I will.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: When did you first notice it?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: It was directly after I had been home last time, and had got back to Paris again. I began to feel the most violent pains in my head--chiefly in the back of my head, they seemed to come. It was as though a tight iron ring was being screwed round my neck and upwards.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Well, and then?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: At first I thought it was nothing but the ordinary headache I had been so plagued with while I was growing up--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Yes, yes--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: But it wasn't that. I soon found that out. I couldn't work any more. I wanted to begin upon a big new picture, but my powers seemed to fail me; all my strength was crippled; I could form no definite images; everything swam before me--whirling round and round. Oh, it was an awful state! At last I sent for a doctor--and from him I learned the truth.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: How do you mean?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: He was one of the first doctors in Paris. I told him my symptoms; and then he set to work asking me a string of questions which I thought had nothing to do with the matter. I couldn't imagine what the man was after--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Well?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: At last he said: "There has been something worm-eaten in you from your birth." He used that very word-- vermoulu .
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Breathlessly.
What did he mean by that?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: I didn't understand either, and begged him to explain himself more clearly. And then the old cynic said--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Clenching his fist.
Oh--!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: What did he say?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: He said, "The sins of the fathers are visited upon the children."
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Rising slowly.
The sins of the fathers--!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: I very nearly struck him in the face--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Walks away across the room.
The sins of the fathers--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Smiles sadly.

Yes; what do you think of that? Of course I assured him that such a thing was out of the question. But do you think he gave in? No, he stuck to it; and it was only when I produced your letters and translated the passages relating to father--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: But then--?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Then of course he had to admit that he was on the wrong track; and so I learned the truth--the incomprehensible truth! I ought not to have taken part with my comrades in that lighthearted, glorious life of theirs. It had been too much for my strength. So I had brought it upon myself!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Oswald! No, no; do not believe it!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: No other explanation was possible, he said. That's the awful part of it. Incurably ruined for life--by my own heedlessness! All that I meant to have done in the world--I never dare think of it again--I'm not able to think of it. Oh! if I could only live over again, and undo all I have done!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: He buries his face in the sofa.
Wrings her hands and walks, in silent struggle, backwards and forwards.
